To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have characterized the two domains of the protein KCTD12 and that we have identified a peptide capable of binding KCTD12 with high affinity.

KCTD12 is composed by two domains, the BTB and the H1, both endowed with a tetrameric organization; the H1 domain shows a β‐structure and is able to bind the BTB domain; the BTB domain is able to bind a GABAB receptor‐related peptide with a very high binding affinity
1) KCTD12 is a tetramer, and 2) the N‐terminal POZ domain is responsible for the tetramerization and for binding the GABAB receptor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of the two folded domains that constitute the KCTD12 protein and their interaction with GABAB2.
the characterization of the structure and function of KCTD proteins.
the characterization of the folded structure and the molecular interactions of the KCTDs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the two domains of KCTDs are endowed with a high degree of structural organization.
KCTD12 is a protein endowed with two folded domains, which are both tetrameric and are able to interact with the GABBR2 receptor and with each other.
KCTD12 has two independent domains with a good affinity for one another and with a tendency to form a tetrameric structure when expressed individually.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have characterized the two structured domains of the GABARAP‐interacting protein KCTD12.
we have characterized the two folded regions of KCTD protein and we have shown how the C‐terminal one interacts with the GABAR2 receptor.
KCTD12 has a compact structure with two structured domains, which are tetrameric and bind to each other and to a GABAB‐related peptide.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have characterized the two folded regions of KCTD proteins, which are involved in the interaction with GABAB2 receptors.
KCTD12 is likely endowed with two interacting structured regions and that the C‐terminal POZ/BTB region is a tetrameric protein.
KCTD12 is a compact tetrameric protein endowed with two folded domains that interact with a high affinity.
